quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When following a car, where in the lane should you ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more than their side mirrors. This position helps you stay visible.

questions.question: What is the minimum requirement for a street-legal motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn signals.
questions.explanation: In North Carolina, a street-legal motorcycle must have a headlight, taillight, brake light, front and rear brakes, turn signals, a horn, and two mirrors.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
When turning, lean in the direction you wish to go.
Avoid dragging your feet on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction you want to go. Do not drag your feet on the road—they could catch on something and cause you to lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: Why should you not ride too far to the right with a sidecar or three-wheeled motorcycle?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side. Riding too far right risks the sidecar leaving the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel could also run off the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group ride?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: Which idea should NOT be used when planning a long group ride?

options.text: The lengths of travel segments should be based on the least experienced rider.
Breaks should be minimized so the riders can get to their destination as soon as possible.
Inexperienced riders should be placed behind the leaders.
The group should maintain a staggered riding formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Breaks should be minimized so the riders can get to their destination as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Plan route length based on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen the best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing while riding to be seen better. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green colors work best. Dark colors are harder to see.

questions.question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance behind other vehicles under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for that weight.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: A passenger on a motorcycle should:

options.text: Mount the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Mount the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as close to the rear of the motorcycle as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mount the motorcycle after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Get on the motorcycle only after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. Sit as far forward as possible without blocking the rider's control. Hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders who have operated the involved motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who have operated the involved motorcycle for less than six months.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle:

options.text: The heavier items should go toward the front.
The heavier items should go toward the rear.
Mounting loads behind the rear axle is recommended.
Lighter items should be stored in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heavier items should go toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of your load. Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Put lighter items behind you.

questions.question: When you are being passed by another vehicle, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle risks collision. Riding on the far side may tempt the driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: How can you discourage another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other vehicles from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a possible cause of a wobble on your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles are usually caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to escape a wobble.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees that they will yield to you.
Doesn't mean that they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean that they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield to you. A driver may look directly at you and still not see you.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move into the portion of the lane farthest from the passing vehicle because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
You may prevent another vehicle from passing you.
The portion of the lane nearest the passing vehicle is better.
You are more likely to experience a wind blast from the passing vehicle on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may tempt the driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When you approach a dangerous area, like an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch lever and brakes. This way, you can react quickly if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What is the correct riding technique?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by moving only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced while turning. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change. Choose a position that gives you the most space and makes other drivers see you better.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane provide for a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths for motorcycles: the left, center, and right parts of the lane.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver in the next lane is too close to the car ahead.
A parked car has someone in the driver's seat.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a pedestrian in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sound your horn to warn vehicles or pedestrians before you pass them, so they don't move into your path. Horn your horn if you see a driver in a parked car, a pedestrian, or a bicyclist in the street as you pass.
